adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsanitized `i.content` from arbitrary RSS/ATOM feeds passed to `TopicEmbed.import` with `cook_method: raw_html` in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35, allowing stored XSS on the forum

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job takes `i.content` from the parsed RSS (`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) and passes it directly to `TopicEmbed.import` without sanitizing HTML. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the post is created via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, and `Post#cook` explicitly returns `raw` when `cook_method` is `raw_html`, bypassing Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The resulting content is then rendered in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` using `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any `<script>` tags or dangerous attributes from the feed would be stored and served to users, enabling stored XSS (even if the feed URL is admin-configured).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `Post#cook` short-circuits with `return raw` for `raw_html` in app/models/post.rb:131, bypassing the sanitizing cook pipeline and `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook)`, yielding unsanitized HTML rendered site-wide

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Post#cook to `return raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which skips the normal cooking/sanitizing pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`) and also skips `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. The new RSS/feed import path (Jobs::PollFeed -> TopicEmbed.import) stores externally-provided HTML into `raw` (via `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` plus appended HTML) and sets `cook_method: :raw_html`, so that HTML will be returned as-is and rendered (e.g., embed/best uses `<%= raw post.cooked %>` and the regular topic rendering will also use `cooked`). There is no sanitization step in TopicEmbed.import for RSS content, making unsanitized HTML/XSS a verifiable risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding `force: true` to already-shipped migration db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 makes `create_table` drop the existing `top_topics` table and silently lose data on re-run; same pattern in the new `create_topic_embeds` migration

adjudication.rationale: `force: true` on `create_table` would indeed drop an existing table *if that migration were executed while the table already exists*. However, the edited `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` migration is an already-versioned migration; in normal Rails operation it will not be re-run on upgraded installs because its version is recorded in `schema_migrations`. If it were re-run (e.g., after a rollback/redo or reset), data would already be lost because `drop_table`/database reset is inherent in those flows. The new `create_topic_embeds` migration also uses `force: true`, but as a new migration it will typically run only once when the table does not yet exist, so no verifiable data-loss defect is introduced by the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic `setnx` followed by separate `expire` in lib/topic_retriever.rb:26-30 can leave the throttle key without expiry forever if the process or Redis fails between calls; should use `SET key 1 NX EX 60`

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, retrieved_recently? sets the throttle key with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then separately calls `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or Redis connection fails after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` is applied, the key can remain without a TTL, causing permanent throttling for that embed_url. This is the classic non-atomic SETNX+EXPIRE issue; using a single atomic command (e.g., `SET key value NX EX 60`) avoids it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` in lib/topic_retriever.rb:47 runs a full synchronous feed fetch and import inline on every cache-miss embed request, letting unauthenticated visitors force repeated whole-feed polls

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` (lib/topic_retriever.rb), when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously before attempting `fetch_http`. `TopicRetriever` is triggered from the embed flow when no `TopicEmbed` exists (EmbedController enqueues `:retrieve_topic`, which calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve`). There is only a per-URL 60s Redis throttle (`retrieved_recently?` uses key `retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so a client can vary `embed_url` (same allowed host) and repeatedly trigger full-feed polling/import work. Since `ensure_embeddable` relies on the request `Referer` header matching `embeddable_host`, an unauthenticated requester can supply that header and enqueue these jobs. This makes repeated whole-feed polls on cache-miss feasible and expensive.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No nil guard in app/models/topic_embed.rb:33 — when an existing `TopicEmbed` row's post has been deleted, `embed.post` is nil and `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and, if the content hash differs, unconditionally does `PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revise!`. There is no guard for `post` being `nil`. The migration enforces `topic_embeds.post_id` is non-null but does not add a foreign key, so a `TopicEmbed` row can exist with a dangling `post_id` (e.g., if a post is hard-deleted or data is otherwise inconsistent). In that case `embed.post` is `nil` and `PostRevisor.new(nil)` will raise, so the finding is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TOCTOU race in app/models/topic_embed.rb:17 between `where(embed_url: url).first` and create against the unique index on `embed_url`, causing `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` for concurrent `RetrieveTopic` jobs on the same URL

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-locking read `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and then, if blank, proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)`. There is a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` (migration `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). With concurrent `RetrieveTopic` jobs for the same URL, both can observe no row and then both try to insert; the second insert will violate the unique index and raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (no rescue/retry shown in the diff). This is a classic TOCTOU race present in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` added to Gemfile:209 but only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` regenerated; the default `Gemfile.lock` is untouched, breaking `bundle install --deployment`/frozen builds

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two new gems to `Gemfile` (`ruby-readability`, `simple-rss`) and updates only `Gemfile_rails4.lock`. There is no corresponding update to the primary lockfile in this diff (i.e., no `Gemfile.lock` change shown). In repos that use a standard `Gemfile.lock` for deployment/frozen installs, changing `Gemfile` without updating that lockfile will cause `bundle install --deployment`/`--frozen` to fail due to lockfile/Gemfile mismatch. The inconsistency (Gemfile changed, only rails4 lock regenerated) is directly observable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` in app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:20 caches a response rendered with `current_user`-dependent `TopicView`, so a shared cache can serve one user's view to another

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is set after building `@topic_view = TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})`, so the content *can* vary based on `current_user` (visibility/permissions). However, the finding’s core claim—“a shared cache can serve one user's view to another”—is not verifiable from this diff because the caching behavior of `discourse_expires_in` (e.g., whether it sets `Cache-Control: public`, varies by cookie, or is private for logged-in users) is defined elsewhere and not shown. Without that, it’s speculative to assert a shared-cache leak introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `contents << "..."` in app/models/topic_embed.rb:12 mutates the caller's string in place, so re-importing the same string appends the "Imported from" footer repeatedly and changes `content_sha1`

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the line `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends to the *same String object* passed by the caller (Ruby `<<` mutates in place). If the caller reuses that `contents` string for another import attempt (e.g., retrying, re-importing, or calling `import` twice with the same variable), the footer will be appended again, and `content_sha1 = Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)` will differ from the previous run, triggering unnecessary updates and producing duplicated "Imported from" footers in the stored post content. This is a concrete correctness hazard introduced by the diff; it can be avoided by duplicating the string (`contents = contents.dup`) or using non-mutating concatenation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `absolutize_urls` in app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 only rewrites hrefs/srcs starting with `/`, leaving document-relative (`foo/bar.jpg`) and protocol-relative (`//host/x`) URLs broken

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, only `href`/`src` values with `start_with?('/')` are rewritten. That means document-relative URLs like `foo/bar.jpg` or `../img.png` are left unchanged and will resolve relative to the Discourse post URL (breaking links/images after import). Also, protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.png` *do* match `start_with?('/')`, but the rewrite strips leading slashes and prefixes the source host, producing an incorrect URL such as `http://sourcehost.com/cdn.example.com/x.png`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test gap in spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:1 — only the settings guard in `execute` is tested; `poll_feed` (feed parsing, nil `content`, link/id fallback), `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, and the referer-host-mismatch rejection branch in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` have no coverage

adjudication.rationale: The added specs primarily cover only guard conditions and delegation, not the newly introduced functional branches. In `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`, tests only assert that `execute` does/doesn’t call `poll_feed`; there are no tests for `poll_feed`’s behavior (SimpleRSS parsing, `link` vs `id` fallback, and the `i.content.scrub` path which could fail if `content` is nil). `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (new, uses `ruby-readability` and `open(url).read`) is not covered by any spec in the diff (the new `topic_embed_spec` covers `.import`, not `.import_remote`). `EmbedController` specs cover missing host, missing referer, and success, but do not cover the `ensure_embeddable` rejection when referer host != `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. This is a concrete, verifiable test coverage gap introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No guard that `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` exists in app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:5, so `comments.appendChild` throws and breaks the host page's other scripts when the element is missing

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, `comments` is assigned from `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then used unconditionally: `comments.appendChild(iframe);`. If the host page does not contain an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` will be `null` and `appendChild` will throw a runtime exception. That’s a concrete defect introduced by the diff (missing null guard). The claim that it breaks the host page’s other scripts is somewhat overstated (it will at least break this embed script and may disrupt execution flow), but the underlying unguarded null dereference is real.
